info.name: Pages
info.summary: Edit, build and publish static websites from Nextcloud
info.description:
# Pages
Pages turns Nextcloud into the editing surface for a static website — Jekyll, Hugo, Eleventy, Astro, VitePress, or plain HTML — and takes it all the way to publication.
## What the app does
- Browses and edits the site source **with Nextcloud's own file API**, so version history, trash, sharing, desktop sync and activity all keep working - Rebuilds the site as you type and shows a live preview in the same page - Reviews the diff and publishes with a single click (or opens a pull request) - Shows the deployment status of the remote CI run
## Deployment model
**This app is the control plane; a companion service is the data plane.**
Nextcloud PHP cannot execute host binaries, and it must not be given the power to start host processes. So the work that needs a real shell — mirroring the source into a working copy, running the site generator, and driving git — is done by `pages-bridge`, a small zero-dependency Python service that runs on the same host.
The administrator installs that service once (the app hands you a ready-to-paste command with the secrets and paths already filled in), and from then on this app owns the configuration: sites are defined here and pushed to the bridge.
Nothing is installed or started behind your back: enabling this app never touches files outside its own data directory.
## Current scope
Targets self-hosted deployments where the administrator can run a small service on the Nextcloud host. Instances that forbid `exec` and cannot run such a service fall back to a read/write editor without build or publish.
